title: How a JointTrajectory looks in Rerun: five ways, with the URDF
kicker: /babble 5 · a real UR5e tour (workspace-dev-029) and a short A to B (workspace-dev-003), the UR5e URDF
brief: Your Nov 24 note: "One thing I don't like right now is how this trajectory looks in rerun … this should basically be the stock trajectory rerun viewer... 100% there should be a urdf showing. Please show 5 different proposals … Please find the previous examples we have done and base yours off of that." Today: a grey tool arc in an empty 3D view and nine separate q/qd/qdd panels. Each proposal is one function, a robot_msgs JointTrajectory + the URDF (+ the tool's path) in, an .rrd out, built on a previous layout, shot in the real Rerun 0.40 web viewer at the same moments.
defaultWhy: R3 · Solo run dashboard scores 95/100: the arm takes 60 % of one screen with faint ghosts at its start and end poses and the tool path solid up to the playhead, beside six named joint strips (degrees, limits, "travel 130° · 38° to limit") and a tool-speed strip, all cursors in step. It grows the Nov 19 Rerun pick (Solo Run Dashboard), and it already ran unchanged on another arm (robotparts' 1-DOF rig, no tool, no limits). What it lacks is speed and acceleration against their limits; the stock version adds R5's at-the-playhead table for that.
decisionHinge: How much the joints' speed and acceleration matter next to the arm. Shift 10 points from "robot first" to "joint motion legible" and R3 still leads (93), but R5's joint cards (92) and R1's question tabs (91) close in: they show q, qd and qdd against limits, which R3 doesn't. If you want the arm alone on screen with the analysis a click away, R2 (evo's tabs) is the cleanest.
invariants: The same two real UR5e trajectories (workspace-dev-029, a 3.2 s multi-waypoint tour; workspace-dev-003, a 1.8 s A to B), the same UR5e URDF (the official collision meshes: Rerun 0.40 can't load the .dae visuals).
One function per proposal: a robot_msgs JointTrajectory + the URDF (+ an optional tool PoseTrajectory) → an .rrd with its blueprint; angles shown in degrees.
Every still from the real Rerun 0.40 web viewer, headless, the playhead set through the viewer's own handle; every recording re-opened by the dispatcher with no ERROR line.
boundary: Prototypes in traj_compare/docs/proposals/rerun-joint-trajectory-2026-11-24/; the .rrd files open in the native viewer too. Nothing is in robot_msgs yet: the pick becomes robot_msgs' stock JointTrajectory viewer next.

variants.name: Stage + questions
variants.thesis: traj_compare's default Rerun layout grown: the URDF arm on a stage, each link in the colour of the joint that drives it, and question tabs beside it — where are the joints, how fast, how hard, where does the tool go.
variants.bestWhen: You want the arm and the joint plots on screen together, with one colour key between them and every limit visible.
variants.losesWhen: Many joints (one plot per joint per tab) or small motions inside wide limits (dev-003's wrist 2 moves 3° in ±360° and reads flat).

decisions.label: Colour key
decisions.value: Each link is tinted with its joint's colour, so the arm and the plots share one key.

decisions.label: Questions
decisions.value: Four tabs: Where are the joints? (°), How fast? (°/s), How hard? (°/s²), Where does the tool go? (mm).

decisions.label: Limits
decisions.value: Dark limit lines with a red strip beyond; titles carry the key number ("wrist 1 · peak 99 % of 180").

decisions.label: At a glance
decisions.value: A table under the arm: each joint's range, limits, peak speed and acceleration.

keepParts: links tinted by their joint's colour
proof: 0 ERROR lines on re-open; exact-time stills 0.400 / 1.800 / 3.200 s

variants.name: evo: a tab per analysis
variants.thesis: traj_compare's evo layout (your Nov 11 pick) grown: Rerun tabs, each full screen — Robot first (the arm, its path so far and still ahead, start and end marked), then Joints, Speed, Acceleration and Data.

variants.losesWhen: You want to see a plot and the arm at the same instant: they are never on screen together.

variants.name: Solo run dashboard
variants.thesis: The Nov 19 Rerun pick (Solo Run Dashboard) grown: one screen, no tabs — the arm large with faint ghosts at its start and end poses and the tool path solid up to the playhead, beside a column of named joint strips and a tool-speed strip.
variants.bestWhen: "What does this whole motion look like, at a glance": the start, the end, where it is now and what every joint is doing, on one screen.
variants.losesWhen: You need speed and acceleration against their limits (logged but not shown), or several trajectories overlaid (target vs real); on a short move the path is small next to the arm.

variants.name: Robot first, numbers at the cursor
variants.thesis: The 3D view is the viewer: the arm fills ~¾ of the screen, the tool path coloured by speed with a bright trail of the last 0.5 s, five faint arms at evenly spaced instants with their times, and every joint's angle as a gauge at the playhead.
variants.bestWhen: A long, spatial motion: the five ghosts and the speed-coloured path tell the whole story in one still.
variants.losesWhen: Short or mostly-rotation moves (dev-003: the ghosts stack up and the path is a stub); no limit lines on the plots; the largest files (~2.4 MB with ghosts).

decisions.label: At the playhead

decisions.label: Plays on open

variants.name: robot_msgs' show(), grown
variants.thesis: The smallest change to what robot_msgs already draws: the URDF arm across the top beside a table of every joint at the playhead, and one card per joint below with q, qd and qdd as % of that joint's own limits on one shared ±100 % axis.
variants.bestWhen: You want every joint's position, speed and acceleration against its limits at a glance, the same way for any arm, with the least new code in robot_msgs.
variants.losesWhen: You want the arm to be the hero: it gets a third of the screen; card legends cover the first ~20 % of each card's time axis.

decisions.label: Cards
decisions.value: One per joint (a 3 × 2 grid for six; adapts to the joint count): q, qd, qdd as % of limit, the ±100 % band shaded, 100 % stated in degrees in the legend.

decisions.label: At the playhead
decisions.value: A table: each joint's q, qd, qdd in degrees and its worst % of limit ("99 qdd").

decisions.label: API
decisions.value: robot= on show / save / recording, and a robot() logger: a URDF path, so robot_msgs gains no dependency.
